Does recovery justify its cost?

Pre-push scenario screen

Observation fees count planner access. Recorder telemetry exists for all policies but is not passed to Blind. Whole-trial timing includes instrumentation and saving the pre-action plan; it is not a pure solver or sensor benchmark.

What this comparison can establish

Three source-bound samples can preserve evidence across an instantaneous callback dropout, while geometry and motion checks reject an inconsistent support state. A missing callback alone does not establish absent physical support. Temporal and Observed differ in history, geometry and fees.

Value uses nine equally weighted analytical scenarios before any first push. Their success fraction is not calibrated recovery confidence. Inspect the native misses avoided and successes sacrificed by its refusals. No controller is automatically promoted.

The first native invocation hit a Windows journal replacement failure. Exact failed evidence remains available; real lock/interruption tests verify the persistence repair. Completed sample arrays and plans from that partial invocation are compared with the unchanged rerun.

The Java-owned path

Requested goal → pre-push value estimate → declined or actual first push → recent contact evidence → saved correction → actual impulse → complete costs and durable outcome.
